title: Strongly multiplicative sets, idempotent localizations, and $S$-prime phenomena
summary: A multiplicative set $S$ of a commutative ring $R$ is strongly multiplicative if every family $(s_i)_{i \in I}$ of elements of $S$ admits a common multiple in $S \cap \bigcap_{i \in I} s_iR$. We combine the structural results on strongly multiplicative sets with their prime-theoretic and module-theoretic applications. We prove that $S$ is strongly multiplicative if and only if localization at $S$ commutes with arbitrary intersections of ideals, if and only if $R_S$ is the localization at an idempotent, and if and only if $D(S)$ is clopen in $\Spec(R)$.
